description: Cross-language wire contract for the X-Grid-* cross-cutting request-context headers (backlog T3-9). TS: apps/workspace/bff/request-context.ts's buildGridRequestContextHeaders(case.input) must equal case.headers. Python: aiq_agent.project_context.GridRequestContext.from_headers(case.headers) must equal the case.input-equivalent fields. A path that forgets to forward one of these headers, or that encodes it differently, fails this fixture instead of silently degrading in production. Base64url payloads below are computed with Node's Buffer.toString('base64url') (unpadded) — the exact encoding server.js / header-encoding.ts / request-context.ts use; the Python decoder re-pads before decoding.

cases.name: full_authenticated_project_context
cases.comment: Every field populated: authenticated org member in a project-scoped chat with org model overrides, a live budget snapshot, org-disabled web_search, and memory reflection on.

cases.name: anonymous_minimal_scope
cases.comment: REQUIRE_AUTH=false / anonymous single-tenant deployment: no org, no user, no project — only the base collection scope and an explicit reflection-off flag survive.

cases.name: project_scoped_no_overrides_no_budget
cases.comment: Authenticated project-scoped request where model-overrides/budget/disabled-sources lookups returned nothing (org has no active override config, budget lookup skipped) — those headers must be OMITTED, not sent empty/null.

envelopeCases.name: signed_envelope_full_context
envelopeCases.comment: Same input as the full_authenticated_project_context case above, minted as the consolidated signed X-Grid-Request-Context envelope instead of individual headers. TS: buildGridRequestContextEnvelope(case.input, case.secret) must equal {header: case.header, signature: case.signature}. Python: GridRequestContext.from_envelope(case.header, case.signature, case.secret) must reproduce the input-equivalent fields, and a wrong secret/signature must make it return None (treated as absent). envelopeJson is the exact raw JSON string signed and base64url-encoded, included for readability/debugging — both sides derive header/signature from it, not the other way around.

envelopeCases.name: signed_envelope_with_federal_state
envelopeCases.comment: Backlog T3-9 follow-up (2026-07-16, user-mandated): jurisdiction rides the envelope as a validated structured field (`federalState`), a parallel channel alongside the unchanged `federal_state=<token>` line inside `projectContext` (still read by the LLM). `federalState` is appended as the LAST payload key (fixed key order) so the signed bytes of every pre-existing case above stay byte-identical after this field was added -- ENVELOPE-ONLY: unlike every other field there is no individual `X-Grid-Bundesland` header (see request-context.ts's module docstring / aiq_agent.project_context's module docstring for why).

envelopeCases.name: signed_envelope_with_conversation_and_issued_at
envelopeCases.comment: ADR-0054: the agent's document route reads the acting user out of the VERIFIED envelope and files in that person's session, so the turn's conversation id and a minting timestamp ride inside the signed bytes. Both are appended AFTER `federalState` in the fixed key order, so every case above keeps byte-identical header/signature. `issuedAt` is epoch milliseconds; the BFF verifier (verifyGridRequestContextEnvelope) refuses an envelope older than six hours and refuses one carrying no issuedAt at all, which is what stops a captured envelope replaying as its user forever. The Python reader keeps accepting envelopes without one -- it has since before the field existed, and stopping would break every in-flight turn.

envelopeCases.name: signed_envelope_with_requester
envelopeCases.comment: Who `userId` is, by name, for the agent prompt's `User:` and `Office:` lines: the requester rides inside the signed bytes (a name shown to the reader never comes from a caller-chosen header), appended LAST after `contextTransport`, so every case above keeps byte-identical header/signature. The BFF fills it from the session the envelope is minted for, live or pinned (`requesterOf`).
